sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: MarkItDown is a small Python tool from Microsoft that converts files such as PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, images and audio into Markdown. It is made for feeding documents into language models and text pipelines.
sixtySeconds.problem: Language models work best with plain text that keeps headings, lists, tables and links. MarkItDown turns office documents and other files into that kind of Markdown, which is also token-efficient.
whoFor: Developers building RAG or document pipelines
Anyone feeding PDFs or Office files to an LLM
Data teams extracting text from mixed file types
Python developers who need a simple converter
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a lightweight, well-known converter that covers many formats from one command or Python call. Its output is meant for machines; for high-fidelity documents meant for people, a dedicated converter may be better.

overview: MarkItDown converts PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images (metadata and captions), audio (metadata and transcription), HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP files, YouTube URLs and EPubs into Markdown. It focuses on keeping structure such as headings, lists, tables and links.

You can use it as a command-line tool or as a Python library. Optional dependencies let you install only the formats you need, for example markitdown[pdf, docx, pptx]. Third-party plugins are supported but disabled by default.

The README notes that image captioning and speech transcription rely on web-hosted services, and that MarkItDown reads files with the permissions of the running process, so inputs should be sanitized in untrusted environments.

steps.title: Clone and install
steps.code:
git clone git@github.com:microsoft/markitdown.git
cd markitdown
pip install -e 'packages/markitdown[all]'
